headline: High-risk shared filesystem and write-capability overlap can enable prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between Plandex and transformers.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex reads and writes a project directory and uses a review-then-apply workflow, while transformers can read/write files and run scripts. If Plandex ingests transformer-generated files or outputs from a shared workspace, attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. The interaction is plausible from the profiles, though not documented as a direct bridge.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory or model-output directory
IF Plandex parses transformer-produced text as task instructions or patches
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Require manual review of any transformer-generated file before Plandex consumes it
Use provenance tags on generated artifacts
requires-engineering: add content-type and source validation between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have filesystem read/write and broad network egress, and Plandex explicitly handles model provider API keys while transformers can process files and call APIs. In a shared workspace, source code or secrets can flow from Plandex into transformer inputs or outbound requests. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or mounted workspace
IF either agent forwards file contents to its backend or external API
mitigations: Use separate OS users
Mount distinct read-only inputs where possible
Keep secrets out of shared directories
Restrict outbound network destinations
requires-engineering: add secret-scanning and redaction before handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can execute shell, modify git state, read/write the filesystem, and supports multiple instances via a shared Plandex server backend; transformers can also execute shell and write files. Concurrent writes to the same repo or model files can race and corrupt state, and the shared backend increases overlap risk. No locking mechanism is documented in the profiles, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or model directory
IF concurrent runs occur without external locking
mitigations: Serialize writes with a single operator
Use separate branches or clones
Disable concurrent instances on shared paths
Add file locks around git and model artifacts
requires-engineering: implement workspace-level coordination primitives

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex’s review-then-apply flow can still treat upstream text as actionable, and transformers can emit scripts, model outputs, or generated text that Plandex may consume. If Plandex accepts those outputs without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect code changes or commands. The profiles suggest a plausible handoff but not a guaranteed one, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF transformers output is fed into Plandex as authoritative input
IF Plandex applies generated patches or commands without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before apply
Validate generated artifacts against tests
Use a second-pass checker for commands and patches
Keep Plandex in review-only mode
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Plandex handles model provider API keys and source code, while transformers touches text, images, audio, video, and multimodal data, but the profiles do not establish a compliance conflict. Because the evidence is sparse, this remains a low-confidence, low-severity gap rather than a breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent without a matching policy
IF one agent is deployed under stricter residency or retention rules than the other
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention settings
Align deployment regions
Review vendor DPAs before use
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing
